text:
ana: Heads up — us-west2 GPU pool is reporting degraded capacity (GPUs unhealthy, ~60% of pods not scheduling). Autoscaler attempted failover to eu-west1 but we’re seeing sustained 5xx for clients still resolving to us-west2. Suspect DNS TTLs and some stale records at large CDNs.

matt: +1 seeing spike in token errors and queue depth. Can we confirm the DNS TTL value for the service record?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-327 — Region failover triggered due to us-west2 GPU degradation. Pager duty: ana, matt.

julia: Lookup shows primary record edgenet.api.redwood-inference.com TTL=300 at Cloud DNS. Some downstream caches still honoring old A-set.

dinesh: Timeline: autoscaler started failing new pods at 17:05 UTC, failover routing kicked at 17:07, but metrics show 40% traffic still hitting us-west2 at 17:12. Likely propagation lag.

laura: Immediate plan: 1) Lower DNS TTL on the record to 60, 2) Push explicit failover A records with higher priority to eu-west1, 3) Purge CDN edges where possible, 4) Notify customers with sticky clients.

matt: I can lower TTL. Running: `gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-prod` then `gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name="edgenet.api.redwood-inference.com." --type=A --ttl=300 --zone=redwood-prod --addresses=34.12.23.45` then `gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name="edgenet.api.redwood-inference.com." --type=A --ttl=60 --zone=redwood-prod --addresses=34.12.23.45` and `gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-prod`.

laura: Also prepare a Route53 change if customers are resolving to ns from partner clouds. I’ll craft a change-batch for backup: `change-batch: {"Changes": [{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet": {"Name":"edgenet.api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.48.100.9"}]}}]}`

ana: @matt once TTL is lowered, we still need to consider EDNS/client OS caching. Set up an intermediate LB rule to respond with 307 to redirect to eu-west1 where possible?

ana (continued): Might be risky for auth tokens but worth discussing.

dinesh: CDN purge kicked: `curl -X POST https://cdn.provider/purge -d '{"url":"https://edgenet.api.redwood-inference.com/*"}'` — provider reports queued. Expect edge flush ~3-6m.

matt: TTL change executed at 17:16 UTC. Cloud DNS returned transaction id tx-9f2e.

deploy-bot: DNS TTL update deployed to zone redwood-prod by matt at 2026-03-18T17:16:22Z.

julia: Quick check: dig +trace shows authoritative answer with TTL=60 now but a few ISP caches still returning TTL 300.

laura: If we still see >20% traffic to us-west2 after 10m, recommended fallback is to withdraw us-west2 A records entirely and rely on eu-west1. We should coordinate client session migration window (30s).

matt: Removing us-west2 IP now as step-down (will do a quick deploy window): `gcloud dns record-sets transaction start ...` then `remove --ttl=60 --addresses=34.12.23.45` then execute.

ana: Be mindful: abrupt IP removal will drop sticky TCP connections for long-lived streams — notify teams.

ops-bot: Change request submitted: CR-2026-881 for emergency DNS rollback + TTL hardset.

dinesh: At 17:25 we see successful drop in error-rate to baseline for 75% of clients; still ~18% behind due to partner CDN caches.

laura: Good. Action items after incident: 1) Set failover-ready TTL default to 60 for all production edge records, 2) Add a playbook step for CDN purge API keys in runbook, 3) Automate a temporary IP-withdrawal policy tied to health-check thresholds.

matt: Agree. Also cost note: shifting live traffic to eu-west1 GPU pools increases unit cost ~15% temporarily — FYI for finance.

ana: Closing loop: purges finished ~17:29, 95th percentile latencies normalized by 17:34. I'll update incident ticket with timeline and TTL recommendation. :white_check_mark:

laura: Marking incident resolved pending post-incident review. Thanks all. :heart:
